metadata.title: Traditional Origami Changing Faces Toy Tutorial
metadata.description:
I have been living in Japan for over 20 years. I love origami and creating designs and patterns. Living in Japan has given me a chance to share things I have learned while living here. So you will find a variety of all of these topics here! 

You can find my digital craft papers and origami projects for sale on ETSY here:
https://www.etsy.com/shop/HappyPuppyTruffles

You can find my book The True Stories of Dream Fairies: Bloom here:
https://books.apple.com/us/author/heather-lynne-shida/id920763042

You can find me on various social media here:
Facebook - https://www.facebook.com/happypuppytruffles
Twitter - https://twitter.com/hptorigami
Instagram - https://www.instagram.com/hptorigami

nodes.plm_action: Create an origami paper fold for the top layer of the cube
nodes.plm_caption: The video is a speeded up video showing how to fold a piece of paper into a dog face. There is a smaller inset video to the right of the person showing the same actions. On the left is a white rectangular object which reads "ORIGAMI RULES!. Lyga & Frelia Daily origami" on it. The paper is green and white in colour. It looks to be held down on an olive green background. There are different actions performed by the person which involves the use of both hands. The hand movements are not in real time. The video ends with the final product of the paper folded into a dog's face.

summary.brief: A speed‑up tutorial folds a green‑and‑white square into a changing‑faces origami toy.
summary.detailed: The video begins with title cards for “Traditional Changing Faces” and an “Origami Rules!” logo, then a hand places a 15 cm green‑and‑white square sheet on an olive‑green table. The paper’s colored side is faced down and it is folded diagonally in both directions to mark the centre. Each corner is then folded into the centre (blintz folds) and unfolded, creating clean creases. After flipping the sheet to show the white side, the right edge is folded toward the centre using the diagonal creases as guides, and the opposite edge is folded the same way, forming a “door‑base” shape. The paper is opened, rotated 90°, and the same edge folds are made on the remaining sides, producing a set of preliminary creases. The model is collapsed by pressing the central creases, pushing the pre‑creased sections inward to create two diamond‑shaped protrusions; the process is repeated on the opposite side to lock the base. Small flaps at the top are folded over, allowing the faces on those flaps to be changed for different expressions. The finished changing‑faces toy is displayed, followed by a closing “See you next time!” screen.

action.detailed: Fold the green‑and‑white square by making diagonal corner folds, bringing each edge to the centre to form a door‑base, collapsing the pre‑creased sections into a compact shape, and then folding the top flaps to create interchangeable facial features, resulting in a changing‑faces toy.

nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows someone making origami on a table. They start with a square piece of paper and fold it into triangles and squares. They then use a stenciled out paper face to fold the origami. A small inset video of the origami is at the top right, while the person is explaining and folding origami at the bottom left. The person is in front of an olive green work surface, while the stenciled out paper face is on a white piece of paper that has a dog's image and text with the words: "Origami Rules! Lyga's daily origami!" The video begins with white screen.
The top right inset video shows hands folding a small piece of green and white paper on a green table. The bottom left inset video shows hands folding a green and white piece of paper. In the center of the video, both hands are in the shot. They start by folding a green and white square piece of paper in half, then diagonally, and then in quarters, finally, they turn the paper sideways and then repeat the folding process, creating four triangles on both sides of the paper. Then, the fingers of the right hand press down the crease that is created by the folds, and the paper begins to bend and change shape.

There is a black and white piece of paper over a green table in the top right, with a black dog drawing and the words: "Origami Rules! Lyga's daily origami! ", where the second line of text also features a black dog on a white background, below that, there is a black "LSI, AMI" to the right of that. In the middle of the paper is a gray, circle-shaped drawing that is cut out.

For the main part of the video, the hands fold the green and white square paper in half, then diagonally, and then in quarters, then turn the paper sideways and the right hand presses down the crease. The hands press down the crease along the top edge and then fold the bottom left and right triangles over, the right hand presses down the crease again. The left hand folds the square in half diagonally, then folds in half again, and finally, the person turns the paper over and folds it in half along the other axis. The fingers press down the crease again. Finally, they turn the paper over, again, and fold it into four triangles on each side. The fingers press down each crease.

On the table, a white square piece of paper is visible, with a small black circle with a thick black line along the top edge, and a small black half circle with a thick black line along the bottom. Below this is a small black semicircle with a thick black line along the bottom. In the top right, there is a black circle with two thick black lines across the top, with two thin black lines along each side, and then at the bottom of the circle a thick black line forming the outline of a dog's face.

At the end of the video, the person presents a completed green and white paper creation with a half triangle face and a half box. The background is a gray table, with a piece of tape at the center that sticks the two separate papers together. On the left side, the words appear: "lyga's daily origami". The video fades away with a gray screen at the end with the words: "See your next video! Lyga's Daily Origami!".

summary.brief: A presenter folds a green‑and‑white square into a Changing Faces origami toy and decorates its flaps with alternating facial expressions.
summary.detailed: The video starts with a green‑and‑white square placed colour‑side down on an olive‑green table. The presenter creases the paper diagonally in both directions to locate the centre, then folds each of the four corners into the centre to form a blintz base. After opening the paper, the four corners are folded inward again to tighten the square. The sheet is flipped to the white side, and the right edge is folded toward the centre using the diagonal creases as guides; the left edge is folded in the same way, creating a “door‑base” shape that is then opened. The paper is rotated 90°, and the same edge folds are repeated on the opposite side, establishing the preliminary creases for the model. The presenter collapses the model by pressing the centre down, forming a small diamond protrusion at the top, rotates the paper another 90° and presses the opposite side down, yielding a compact three‑dimensional figure with two triangular flaps. Simple eyes and mouths are drawn on the visible sections, and each flap is folded over in opposite directions to reveal different facial expressions, demonstrating the toy’s changing‑faces feature. The completed origami piece is held up for the camera, showing both sides of the toy.

action.detailed: Fold the green‑and‑white square by first making diagonal creases, pulling each corner to the centre, folding the right and left edges toward the centre using the diagonal guides, repeating after a 90° turn, pressing the centre down to form a diamond, turning 90° and pressing the opposite side, then draw faces on the flaps and fold them over to create alternating expressions.

summary.brief: The presenter folds a green‑and‑white square into a Changing‑Faces origami toy, draws simple faces on its flaps, and shows the finished pieces.
summary.detailed: Beginning with the coloured side down, the presenter folds the square paper diagonally both ways to locate the centre, then folds each corner into the centre (blintz folds) and sharpens the creases. After unfolding, the paper is turned over; the right edge is folded toward the centre using the diagonal creases as guides, followed by the left edge, forming a “door‑base” shape. The paper is opened, rotated 90°, and the same pair of side folds are made on the opposite side, creating a set of preliminary creases. The model is then collapsed by pressing the central flaps down to a small diamond‑shaped base, and the same pressure is applied on the other side, completing the compact origami toy. Simple eyes and mouths are drawn on the small flaps, and each flap is folded over in turn to produce different facial expressions such as winking, sleeping, smiling or sad faces. Finally, two small pieces—one white with a drawn face and one green box—are placed side by side on a grey surface, pressed flat, and the white piece is flipped to reveal its hidden face, demonstrating the finished Changing‑Faces toy.

action.detailed: Using both hands, fold the square paper diagonally both ways, bring each corner to the centre, unfold, turn the paper over, fold the right and left edges toward the centre using the diagonal creases as guides, repeat on the opposite side, rotate 90°, collapse the model by pressing the central flaps flat into a diamond shape, draw simple eyes and mouths on the small flaps, and fold each flap over to display different facial expressions.

summary.brief: Hands fold a square sheet into a Changing Faces origami toy and add interchangeable facial expressions.
summary.detailed: The presenter begins with a 15 × 15 cm square of green‑white paper, color side down. Diagonal folds are made both ways to locate the centre, then each corner is folded to that centre to create a blintz base. The paper is opened, turned over to the white side, and the right edge is folded toward the centre using the diagonal creases as guides; the left edge is folded the same way. The model is opened again, rotated 90°, and the side folds are repeated, producing the preliminary creases needed for the next step. By pressing down in the middle the model collapses into a small diamond shape at the top, and the two side flaps are flattened to form two square sections. Small faces are drawn on these sections, and each flap is folded over so that different eyes and mouths appear, allowing the toy to show normal, winking, sleeping, smiling, or sad expressions. The finished Changing Faces origami toy is displayed at the end of the segment.

summary.brief: The presenter folds a green‑and‑white square into the pre‑creased base for the Changing Faces origami toy.
summary.detailed: Starting with a 15 cm square of green‑and‑white paper placed color‑side down, the presenter folds the sheet diagonally in both directions to mark the center. The paper is then opened and turned over so the colored side faces up. Each of the four corners is folded into the center, forming a blintz base. The sheet is reopened, and the right edge is folded toward the center using the diagonal creases as guides, then the left edge is folded the same way, creating a “door‑base” shape. The paper is rotated 90°, the opposite edges are folded similarly, and the model is opened again. Finally, the side flaps are pushed together toward the middle and pressed to collapse the model into a small diamond‑shaped pre‑creased base, completing the basic structure of the Changing Faces toy.

action.detailed: Fold the square diagonally both ways, bring all four corners to the center, flip the paper over, fold each side edge to the center using the diagonal creases as guides, rotate the sheet 90°, repeat the side folds, then press the central flaps inward to collapse the model into a diamond‑shaped base.

summary.brief: The tutorial shows how to make the Changing Faces origami display different facial expressions by folding its eye and mouth flaps.
summary.detailed: The presenter displays the completed Changing Faces paper toy on a gray tabletop and then folds the small pre‑creased flaps that form the eyes and the mouth. Folding the upper eye flaps down creates a winking eye, while folding them up produces a sleeping eye. Folding the lower mouth flap down gives a normal smile, folding it further down reveals teeth, and folding it up makes a sad mouth. By combining these up‑and‑down folds, a variety of funny faces are demonstrated before the paper is set flat at the end of the segment.

summary.brief: The presenter folds a green‑and‑white square, creates a blintz, flips it, makes door‑base edge folds on both sides and repeats them after a 90° turn.
summary.detailed: Starting with the green‑side down, the demonstrator folds the square diagonally in both directions to locate the centre, then opens the sheet so the green side faces up. Each of the four corners is folded inward to meet the centre, forming a blintz shape. The paper is unfolded and turned over to show the white side. The right edge is folded toward the centre, using the existing diagonal creases as guides, and the left edge is folded similarly, creating a door‑base pair of folds. The model is opened again, rotated 90°, and the same pair of side folds are performed on the new orientation, establishing the preliminary creases needed for the next stage of the origami toy.

action.detailed: Make diagonal creases both ways, open the sheet, flip it over, fold each corner to the centre, unfold and flip to the opposite side, fold the right and left edges toward the centre as door‑base folds, open the model, rotate it 90°, repeat the side folds on the new orientation, and press the resulting creases.

nodes.plm_caption: This video captures someone folding origami with a square green paper. He folds it into four triangles and makes two creases. Then he flips it over and folds the other side into three equal sections. He then makes a long, thin crease down the centre. He then continues folding it into two sections before flipping it over again and folding another crease. They then unfolds it and opens it out again. It looks like they are making a dog house. It also looks like it could also be used as an envelope. He's making lines down both sides of the paper.

summary.brief: The presenter folds a square green‑and‑white sheet, makes centered edge folds and a diamond base to shape the Changing Faces origami toy.
summary.detailed: Starting with a partially folded square, the hands open the model and flip it to show the white side. The right edge is folded toward the centre, using the diagonal creases as guides, and a matching fold is made on the left edge. The paper is then unfolded, rotated 90°, and the top and bottom edges are folded inward in the same way, sharpening all creases. After reopening the sheet, a small central square appears; the sides are pushed together toward the centre, flattening the square into a diamond shape. The model is turned another 90°, the opposite sides are pushed in similarly, and the central diamond is pressed down to create two folded sections, completing the origami figure. Throughout, both hands manipulate the paper on a gray tabletop while a small inset window shows the same actions from another angle.

action.detailed: Fold the right edge toward the centre, repeat on the left, unfold and rotate the sheet, fold the top and bottom edges toward the centre, then open the model and push the central square inward to form a diamond and collapse the paper into its final shape.

summary.brief: The hands press and fold the pre‑creased paper to form the diamond‑shaped base of the Changing Faces origami toy.

nodes.plm_caption:
This video features two images juxtaposed with each other, the first is a hand holding a white square sheet of paper. The second is a close-up of the white paper and a hand in which the person is demonstrating how to crease the paper.  The background is a grey surface.
The person starts with their left hand positioned over the top of the paper, their fingers placed evenly on the paper to anchor it in place. Their right index and thumb fingers lift slightly above the paper. They use the index finger on their right hand to point out a crease in the top right of the paper, as they slowly move the finger towards the bottom right. As the finger reaches the bottom right, they remove their index finger from the paper. The hand then moves the right edge of the paper backwards at a quick pace, the fingers lifting slightly above the paper's surface, to apply pressure against the table. The fingers come back down to the top of the paper.
The person in the second frame holds both hands on the paper, the right thumb and index fingers are underneath the paper, the left thumb and index fingers are resting on the paper, and their two middle fingers are extended on top of the paper, as they move their right thumb and middle finger across the bottom edge of the paper. The left thumb and index fingers are then lifted off the paper as the right hand lifts it off the table at a slow pace.

summary.brief: The presenter creates a crease along the right side of a white sheet, folds the edge, then slides along the bottom and lifts the paper upward and slightly to the right.
summary.detailed: A white square rests on a grey tabletop. The left hand lays flat over the top of the paper to hold it in place while the right hand’s index finger traces a line from the top‑right corner toward the bottom‑right corner, forming a crease. After the finger is removed, the right hand pushes the right edge backward quickly to sharpen the fold. The hands then reposition: the right thumb and index finger go beneath the paper, the left thumb and index stay on top, and both middle fingers are extended over the surface. The right thumb and middle finger slide along the bottom edge as the left hand releases its grip, and the right hand lifts the paper upward and a little to the right, moving it toward the lower‑left corner. A small inset window shows a similar hand motion in a close‑up view.

action.detailed: Hold the sheet with the left hand, use the right index finger to mark a crease down the right side, press the right edge back to set the fold, then slide the right thumb and middle finger along the bottom edge while lifting the paper upward and slightly to the right.

The person is holding the paper with both hands, in a landscape orientation. The right hand is folded on the white side while the left is folded on the green side. Their hands move on to fold the green and white sides together in a vertical direction, making sure the crease and the white and green are aligned. Then they unfold the paper and flip it to the opposite side on the green part and the white part. On the other picture there is a smaller version of the person folding the paper along the green and white lines. The hand lines to the top and bottom side then moves to the green and white side before going to the left and then the right. They repeat this process until the folded paper is in their desired orientation.
On the left side, in the top corner there is a white sticker with a dog logo, saying "Origami rules!'. Underneath it there is another white square with the date "1st July 2015'. In the top right is a smaller inset picture where the hands and fingers are visible. There is a grey background with a crease in it. The video is sped up.

summary.brief: The presenter forms a door‑base fold, reopens the paper, rotates it 90°, and repeats the fold to set preliminary creases.
summary.detailed: Holding the green‑and‑white square, the presenter aligns the edges and makes a crisp central crease. One side is folded inward so the two flaps meet like closed doors, creating a door‑base. The paper is then unfolded, turned 90° and the opposite side is folded inward in the same way, producing a second set of preliminary creases that will guide the next collapse step.

action.brief: Create door‑base folds and set preliminary creases
action.detailed: Align the edges, crease the center line, fold one side inward to form a door‑base, unfold the paper, rotate it 90°, then fold the opposite side inward to establish the preliminary creases.

nodes.plm_caption:
The video features the hands of a human folding a green and white piece of paper. The top screen is placed horizontally so the fingers are placed on it. The left screen is the normal video while the top right screen is the hand holding the paper down.
At the start the person lines up both hand by pushing the green paper back and forth to crease it. The green part moves to the left while the white part moves to the right, then goes the other way.

The person moves their hands away and starts to turn the paper so the top section is facing to the camera.

The person folds the paper towards the center to line up with the crease that was made earlier. This creates a line between the two sections. the person presses it together and it goes back to look like it was before folding.

They turn the paper back and look to reveal the new crease. As it moves from left to right, the edges match up and they use a flat finger to press it.
At the end, they start to unfold the bottom half of the paper to create a triangle, and start to lift the other half upwards. As the video ends, the left hand is still on the bottom half while the right hand is lifting up the other half in the right side of the screen.

The grey background of the video moves slightly as the paper is being moved. It is a soft grey with a slight wave pattern running across the video.

summary.brief: Hands crease, fold, and rotate the paper to make intersecting door‑base creases, then fold a triangle and reveal the opposite side.
summary.detailed: The presenter lines up the green‑and‑white square, presses a central crease, folds one side over the crease and then the opposite side to form a door‑base, unfolds the sheet and rotates it 90°, repeats the same door‑base folds on the new orientation to create perpendicular creases, folds a lower corner up into a triangular flap, presses a crease on that flap, and slides the paper so the white side is shown beneath the folded triangle.

action.detailed: Align the sheet, crease the center line, fold each side inward to form a door‑base, unfold, rotate the paper 90°, repeat the door‑base folds on the new orientation, then fold a triangular flap, press its crease and slide the paper to reveal the opposite side.

summary.brief: The hands crease and fold the paper into a door‑base shape and then fold it in half.
summary.detailed: With the paper positioned white‑side up, the maker lines up the pre‑creased edges and presses one flap flat using three fingers. summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video begins with title cards for “Traditional Changing Faces” and an “Origami Rules!” logo, then a hand places a 15 cm green‑and‑white square sheet on an olive‑green table. The paper’s colored side is faced down and it is folded diagonally in both directions to mark the centre. Each corner is then folded into the centre (blintz folds) and unfolded, creating clean creases. After flipping the sheet to show the white side, the right edge is folded toward the centre using the diagonal creases as guides, and the opposite edge is folded the same way, forming a “door‑base” shape. The paper is opened, rotated 90°, and the same edge folds are made on the remaining sides, producing a set of preliminary creases. The model is collapsed by pressing the central creases, pushing the pre‑creased sections inward to create two diamond‑shaped protrusions; the process is repeated on the opposite side to lock the base. Small flaps at the top are folded over, allowing the faces on those flaps to be changed for different expressions. The finished changing‑faces toy is displayed, followed by a closing “See you next time!” screen.
